transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Tamara Li (CISO - Ridgeview), Daniel Reed (Eng Manager), Priya Sharma (Security Architect)

Summary (auto-generated): Weekly POC security sync focusing on SSO, audit logs, data retention and SOC2 evidence.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. This is Maya from Redwood, Carlos is our SE, we'll go through the security items you flagged last week and confirm next steps.
[00:10] Tamara Li: Thanks Maya. Quick note, we've got a tight timeline for the pilot compliance review, so want to make sure SSO and audit logs are squared away.
[00:18] Carlos Nguyen: Yep, understood. We pulled the pilot logs and did an initial pass on retention. Quick heads up - some of the terminology in our notes might be off, the transcribe often writes K M S spaced out, or S A M L, sorry if that shows up weirdly.
[00:30] Priya Sharma: No worries, just want clarity on two main things: one, SSO - Okta integration flows and session lifetime; two, audit logs - retention and ability to export to our SIEM.
[00:40] Maya Patel: Great. On SSO, standard flow is SAML 2.0 with Okta, we support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated. Carlos, do you want to run through the metadata we need?
[00:47] Carlos Nguyen: Sure. For a basic Okta SAML setup we need the IdP metadata XML, ACS URL which we'll provide, and attribute mappings for email and user id. We can also support SCIM if you want automated provisioning, but for the pilot many customers start with SAML only.
[00:59] Daniel Reed: SCIM would be nice long-term but for the POC we'll stick to SAML. Question - session TTLs: can we enforce session length at SSO level or do we need token revocation?
[01:10] Carlos Nguyen: You can enforce session TTLs in Okta; Redwood's tokens adhere to the session created by SAML assertion. We also support short-lived API tokens and you can rotate them via KMS. We're using customer-managed keys for Private deployments, hosted mode uses Redwood KMS by default but we support customer KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for the private option.
[01:28] Tamara Li: Good. For the pilot we prefer the hosted control plane but with a customer KMS if possible. Is that available in the dedicated pilot?
[01:35] Maya Patel: For the pilot on hosted we can do envelope encryption with a customer-managed key in AWS KMS - it's a supported pattern. If you go Private/on-prem later, you get full KMS control. We'll confirm specifics in the security pack.
[01:46] Priya Sharma: On audit logs, we saw sample logs in the dashboard but need to confirm retention and fields. We need immutable logs for 90 days and export to our Splunk instance.
[01:56] Carlos Nguyen: Right. Current pilot workspace defaults to 30 days but we can increase to 90 days. We also have streaming export - either S3 export or syslog/HTTPS push to your SIEM. For Splunk specifically we can push via HTTP Event Collector or S3 ingestion.
[02:10] Tamara Li: Are the logs PII redacted by default? We can't have raw PHI in the logs for the health pilot.
[02:16] Carlos Nguyen: By default we capture audit metadata (user, API call, timestamp, model, route) and not full user prompt text in the audit logs. However, request/response bodies can be captured depending on your workspace settings. We have a redaction config that strips or hashes PII before logs are stored or exported. For pilot I can enable a redaction pipeline that masks email, SSNs, and names.
[02:34] Priya Sharma: That's important - can you document what fields are masked and provide an example?
[02:38] Carlos Nguyen: Yes, I'll add a short doc with examples. I'll also include the regex patterns we use for detection; caveat - regex-based detection isn't perfect but works for common patterns. For stricter needs we recommend application-level tokenization.
[02:52] Daniel Reed: For data retention, what's the policy around prompt / response storage? We need to know retention windows per environment.
[02:58] Maya Patel: Prompt and response retention is configurable per workspace. For the pilot we can set 30/90/365 days. We typically recommend storing minimal artifacts for evaluation and using ephemeral storage for production if you don't need transcripts. Also you can configure retention at the project route level.
[03:12] Tamara Li: SOC2 - you mentioned you'd share the Type II report? We need audit evidence for our compliance team.
[03:18] Maya Patel: Absolutely. I'll share the SOC2 Type II report and the security pack (encryption at rest, in transit, pen test summaries, ISO if applicable). We'll send via a secure link - we'll include redacted scopes as needed.
[03:28] Priya Sharma: Do you provide mapping of controls to your implementation?
[03:31] Maya Patel: Yes, we have an attached controls mapping doc that maps SOC2 controls to Redwood features and policies. I'll include that.
[03:37] Tamara Li: Excellent. One more - audit trails: can we get user-level session tracing and impersonation logs? Need to show access patterns for audits.
[03:45] Carlos Nguyen: We capture user session start/stop, token issuance, role changes and admin actions. Impersonation events are flagged. We can also add trace IDs to requests so you can correlate logs across services.
[03:55] Daniel Reed: On the technical side, small note - earlier the performance team ran a KV cache test, the transcript shows K V cache as two letters, but results are fine. Any operational implications for the pilot when enabling KV cache and prefix caching?
[04:07] Carlos Nguyen: KV cache is safe for the pilot; it's per-instance and doesn't expose other customers. For compliance it's treated like ephemeral state and is not written to persistent logs unless you opt-in for debugging traces.
[04:18] Tamara Li: Good. Can we talk briefly about legal/procurement items we might need during the POC? Specifically data processing addendum and standard contractual clauses for EU users.
[04:27] Maya Patel: Yes, we have a DPA and SCCs available. I'll share links in the security pack. For the pilot, we can sign the DPA and use standard SCCs if you need EU data residency.
[04:36] Priya Sharma: Also, who is the contact for incident response and how fast do you provide logs on request?
[04:41] Carlos Nguyen: We have an incident response SLA in our enterprise package. For pilots we'll commit to a standard timeline - initial acknowledgement within 2 hours and log support within 24 hours for high-severity. I'll confirm exact wording in the pack.
[04:53] Tamara Li: Can you walk through an example of exporting audit logs to Splunk?
[04:58] Carlos Nguyen: Sure. Option A: configure S3 export on schedule (we push daily compressed JSON) and you ingest into Splunk. Option B: configure an HTTPS push to your HEC endpoint; we can stream events in near real-time. For the POC we usually demo S3 export since it's simpler.
[05:14] Daniel Reed: We'll probably start with S3 push and then test HEC if we need real-time.
[05:18] Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable. Carlos, please include step-by-step for S3 setup and sample payload.
[05:22] Carlos Nguyen: Will do.
[05:24] Tamara Li: One nit - audit logs in the UI only sample things, but our auditors want raw events; is there a way to pull raw event granularity?
[05:31] Carlos Nguyen: Yes, raw event export gives request id, timestamp, user, route, model, and optionally the prompt/response depending on your retention config. For PHI concerns, we'll have redaction on for exported payloads unless you explicitly enable full payload export.
[05:45] Priya Sharma: Can you confirm who will have access to the exported S3 bucket? We need to ensure it's encrypted and IAM locked to our account.
[05:51] Carlos Nguyen: The S3 export can write to your bucket using a customer-managed role. We don't retain the bucket credentials. Objects are server-side encrypted; you can require SSE-KMS with your key.
[06:03] Tamara Li: Great. Any blockers on our side to get SAML test working?
[06:07] Maya Patel: We just need the IdP metadata and a test user. Tamara, if you can send that we can spin up the test in under an hour.
[06:15] Tamara Li: I'll send Okta metadata and a test account after this call.
[06:19] Daniel Reed: Regarding retention config, can you schedule a short change freeze after enabling 90-day retention so we can validate logs?
[06:25] Carlos Nguyen: We can enable 90-day retention immediately on the pilot workspace and maintain that for the duration of the pilot. I'll note the change freeze window in the action items.
[06:33] Maya Patel: Quick recap of next steps: Maya will share SOC2 and security pack; Carlos will enable 90-day audit retention and share export docs; Tamara to send Okta metadata and Splunk endpoint info; schedule a demo for log export next week. Any other items?
[06:47] Priya Sharma: Please also include the redaction examples.
[06:50] Carlos Nguyen: Adding redaction examples to the doc.
[06:53] Tamara Li: That covers it for me. Thanks.
[06:55] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and a secure link to SOC2.
[07:00] (call ends)

Notes: Transcription has occasional spacing of acronyms (S A M L, K M S) and some speaker labels may be generic. Shared artifacts referenced: "SOC2_TypeII_Redwood.pdf" (link to be provided), "okta_metadata_example.xml" (customer to provide), "audit-export-sample.json" (SE to provide).
